title: Replicating Oversight Subversion in Petri Across Open Models with API Constraints

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: oversight subversion is among the most dangerous scheming behaviors. Establishing its base rate across open models is critical for deployment risk assessment and policy decisions.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: Petri is open-source, so running existing seed instructions against open models is feasible. Categorizing subversion behaviors requires judgment but not advanced ML skills.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: run existing Petri seeds against two open models, compare elicitation rates, categorize behavior types. The framework and seeds already exist, so the work is execution and analysis.

evidence: Petri (Anthropic, Oct 2025) tested 14 frontier models on oversight subversion with 111 seed instructions, successfully eliciting oversight subversion behaviors.
Petri 2.0 (Jan 2026) expanded to 10 target models with improved eval-awareness mitigations and new scenarios.
The Petri framework is open-source and designed to work with any model including open-weight models, so the infrastructure for this replication already exists.
METR conducted preliminary evaluations of DeepSeek and Qwen models finding capabilities similar to frontier models from late 2024.
However, a focused comparative study of oversight subversion rates specifically across open-weight models with API constraints has not been published as a standalone study.

relevance_scores.citation: Anthropic 2025 - Petri: An open-source auditing tool
